lines.text: The dead walk in the Old Graveyard, {name}. They haven't done that in a hundred years. The Guild wants to know why. So do I.
You've seen them, then. Skeletons in the old King's colours. Aldous the sexton still lives out there. If anyone knows why, he does.
The King is down, and the road north is open. Whatever he said at the end, I've written it down. The Guild will want to hear it.
Maud has my letter, then. Twenty years she's kept that moor for the Guild. If she says the road is bad, it's bad.
The bridge is free for the first time in my life. Maud writes that the crates went up the pass, to our own lodge. Corvin will know what's in them. Corvin knows everything.
The dragon. Dead. I've written it three times, and it still looks wrong on the page. The Guild will deal with Corvin. Sit down, {name}. Eat something.
Forty years I've burned charcoal in these woods. Goblins were always here. Never this many, and never this bold.
A woodcutter's {son|daughter|child}, are you? Then you've heard it too. The woods have gone quiet. The birds left first.
They're not raiding, {name}. They're running. Something up north drives them south, and they push everything before them.
Heard the King fell. The goblins heard too. They're still running, though. Whatever's up north didn't fall with him.
The goblins went home, {name}. North, back where they came from. I never thought I'd miss the noise.
Mind the graves, {name}. Fifty years I've kept them. I never thought I'd have to keep them shut.
Those are his own guard, you know. They followed him to the Peak and back, and into the ground. They wake when he wakes.
You laid him down again. Thank you. He spoke at the end, didn't he? He always did talk of the dragon.
The graves are quiet. All of them. He held it a hundred years, and you finished it. He can rest now. So can I.
Nobody finds this cove by chance, friend. So who sent you? No, don't tell me. I sell secrets. I don't buy them.
Coast folk. You'll keep your mouth shut, then. Coast folk always do.
The King's dead? Then the north road is open, and my old cargo moves again. Crates for the Peak, friend. Don't ask what's in them.
You've made a name. The captain who sank off my jetty had a name too. Want to hear it? It'll cost you nothing. This time.
The bridge is free, the toll is gone, and my crates? Nobody wants them now. Bad times for an honest smuggler.
A dead dragon. Do you know what a dragon's scale sells for, friend? No? Then you'll sell me yours cheap.
You're Odda's {lad|lass|friend}? Good. The moor eats people who walk it alone. Wolves by day, the pale ones by night, and bandits whenever they like.
A hunter's apprentice. Then read the tracks on the moor: everything runs south. Even the wolves look over their shoulders.
Fifty bandits, and not one of them carried a crate for the high road. They rob our carts and wave those through. Someone pays them better than we do.
The Chieftain's dead, and the bridge is free. The carts roll again. Only the crates stopped. Funny, that.
I lit every watch-fire on the moor tonight, {name}. Not for a warning. Just because.
Mind the arches, friend. Spiders up top, trolls down below, and the Chieftain in the middle with his hand out. I pay. Everybody pays.
From the Copper Hills? My mother hauled ore out of there. You know a heavy load when you see one. I've hauled some heavy loads.
All right. You've earned it. I hauled a cage over this bridge. Iron, big as a barn. The Chieftain counted the gold twice and waved me through.
No toll! I crossed four times today just to feel it. Where the cage went? Up the pass, friend. To the lodge. I only drive the cart.
Welcome to the lodge, {name}! Warm beds, a hot forge and the best stew north of the river. The Guild's heroes never pay here. I insist.
A tavern cook! Then you'll forgive my stew. Take the kitchen whenever you like. A lodge lives on its cooks.
The mules move again, thanks to you. My men on the Peak will eat well this month. Surveyors, {name}. Brave men. Cold work.
So the old woman on the Peak talks. Yes, a cage. Do you know what a live dragon is worth, {name}? Kings would bow to the man who owns one.
You killed it. The only one in the world, and you killed it. The Guild will send for me now. I hope it was worth it, {name}.
Another one from the lodge? No. You walk different. Keep your voice down. It sleeps lightly now.
Smith's hands. Good. My grandfather wrote that only crushing blows go through its scales. He didn't bring a hammer. Don't make his mistake.
My grandfather went up to kill it and never came down. My mother watched it all her life, and now I do. It slept a hundred years. Then the lodge men came with hammers.
It's over. A hundred years of watching, and it's over. Come and see what I found behind its bed, {name}. Then tell me it's over.

campLines.text: The King, {name}? Under the hills we'll drink to that.
The woods feel lighter since the King fell. Not the goblins, mind.
They say the river runs clearer with the King gone. The fish don't care. I do.
You walked soft and hit hard. The King never heard you coming.
Full plate, they said, and you cracked it. Bring me a piece. I'd like to see that steel.
The King's Bane eats free tonight, {name}.
One king down. Steps made that, {name}. Steps and talents.
The Chieftain? The ogres up north fear you now, {name}. Under the hills, we drink to that too.
They say the bridge is free. I'd like to see the pines past it before I'm too old.
Under the bridge the trout bite again. Ogres scare fish, you know. Everyone forgets that.
An ogre is a big target. Still, you hit it where it hurt. Good.
Layered leather and hide, they say, and you found the gaps. I'd have liked to see that.
Ogre-slayer! I'll put something big on the fire, {name}. Something ogre-sized.
Two bosses down. Feel the talents settle, {name}? That's the road under your feet.
A dragon. Under the hills they'll sing of you for a hundred years, {name}. Badly, but loud.
The woods are full of birds again. They came back first. I noticed.
The lake is so still this morning, {name}. As if it knows.
I taught you to walk soft. You walked soft all the way to a dragon. I'm proud of you.
Heavy as a cathedral door, the hunter wrote. And you broke it. Bring me a scale, {name}. Just one.
Dragonslayer at my fire! Sit. Eat. Nobody pays tonight, not even Jory.
Thirty levels, {name}, and a dragon at the top. Steps did that. Your steps.

pages.title: The Guild's charter
pages.text: Pinned to the notice board: "The Guild takes any hand that can hold a blade or a pick. Pay in coin, or pay in stories. The lands south of the river are ours to keep."

pages.title: Odda's ledger
pages.text: A new line in Odda's neat hand: "{name}: the Graveyard King, laid to rest. His last words: it wakes. Sent word north."

pages.title: Goblin tally
pages.text: A stick dropped by a goblin. Rows of little running feet are carved on it, and above them a great burning eye.

pages.title: Pell's story
pages.text: What Pell told you: "My grandfather was a boy the year the King rode north. The woods burned to the river that summer. Now the goblins smell the same smoke he did."

pages.title: Hunter's book, page 1
pages.text: A page torn from a hunter's book: "Day one. The King rides north with three hundred spears. I go with them, to see a dragon and live to write of it."

pages.title: The sexton's ledger
pages.text: The first page of an old ledger: "Buried this day: His Majesty, in his plate, with his guard around him. The dragon lives. May the graves stay shut."

pages.title: The King's last words
pages.text: As the King falls, a voice rises from the helm: "It wakes. A hundred years I held it. It wakes..."

pages.title: Aldous's story
pages.text: What Aldous told you: "Fifty years I've heard them under the turf, turning. Waiting for him. I used to think it was the wind."

pages.title: Hunter's book, page 2
pages.text: "The King swore over his father's grave: no dragon would burn his lands while he drew breath. He kept his word. In his way."

pages.title: Miner's carving
pages.text: Cut into the rock above the old copper vein: a dragon with its wings spread, and under it one word: HIDE.

pages.title: Hunter's book, page 3
pages.text: "We dug in under the hills to wait out its flight. The miners say the rock stayed warm for a week after it passed."

pages.title: Reed charm
pages.text: A charm of woven reeds on a post at the shore: "For the eleven who came home."

pages.title: Hunter's book, page 4
pages.text: "We came back across the lake, eleven of three hundred, with the King on a shield. The water showed us what we had become."

pages.title: Smuggler's manifest
pages.text: A manifest, the ink run: "Twelve crates, sealed. Rope, salt, lamp oil. One cage, large, iron, empty."

pages.title: The captain's log
pages.text: Log of the Gull, the last entry: "Cargo for the Peak, paid in old gold. The crew won't say whose. Storm rising. If this book is found, burn the manifest."

pages.title: Jory's story
pages.text: What Jory told you: "The Gull sank off this jetty with cargo for the Peak, paid in old gold. Whose gold? Ask the King. Oh, wait."

pages.title: Odda's letter
pages.text: Pinned up in the outpost, in Odda's neat hand: "Maud: the King is down. His last words were 'it wakes'. Watch the high road. I'm sending {name}."

pages.title: Hunter's book, page 5
pages.text: "Twenty years on, I go north again, alone. The King held it in his way. I mean to end it in mine."

pages.title: Maud's story
pages.text: What Maud told you: "The bandits rob every cart on the ridge road. All but the sealed crates for the high road. Those they wave through, hats off."

pages.title: Bandits' ledger
pages.text: A greasy book in a bandit camp: "Carts robbed: 31. Crates for the high road: let pass, by order. Paid in old crowns, the King's face on them."

pages.title: Miner's slate
pages.text: Scratched on a slate by the vein: "Iron for chains. Forty fathoms, links thick as a wrist. Ordered from up the pass. No name given."

pages.title: Toll board
pages.text: Carved over the arch: ONE TOLL. NO RETURNS. Under it, in fresh chalk: "Crates for the high road go free."

pages.title: Hunter's book, page 6
pages.text: "The ogres took my coin and laughed. The trolls took my mule. I went on with what I could carry."

pages.title: Tobin's story
pages.text: What Tobin told you: "A cage, iron, big as a barn. Chains on a second cart. The Chieftain bit every coin. Old crowns, from before my grandmother was born."

pages.title: The Chieftain's hoard
pages.text: Under the Chieftain's seat: a heap of old crowns with the King's face, and a scrap of the toll book: "Cage and chains, for the high road. Paid in full. Sealed at the lodge."

pages.title: The lodge's guest book
pages.text: On the first page: "Welcome to the Guild lodge. Warm beds, a hot forge and no questions. Corvin, lodge master."

pages.title: Hunter's book, page 7
pages.text: "The pass is full of our dead. They stand where they fell, in their shrouds, and still guard the King's war chest."

pages.title: The King's war chest
pages.text: Behind the shrouded dead stands an iron chest with the King's seal. Its lock is broken, and it is empty. Fresh boot prints lead down to the lodge.

pages.title: Chalk at the shaft
pages.text: Chalked at the shaft head: "Mithril for the lodge. Forty bars, cast thick. What for? Don't ask, says the lodge master."

pages.title: The lost lamp
pages.text: A miner's lamp, its glass scratched by an old hand: "It sleeps above us. Dig quiet."

pages.title: The empty cage
pages.text: A cage of iron and mithril, as big as a barn, chained to the rock. Its door is torn off. Claw marks run down the bars.

pages.title: The foreman's letter
pages.text: "To Master Corvin: the beast stirs under the hammers. The men won't go near it. Send more chain, or send us home."

pages.title: Nessa's story
pages.text: What Nessa told you: "The King held it asleep for a hundred years. When he fell, the hammers woke it. Corvin wanted it in a cage. Nothing that size goes in a cage."

pages.title: The old scale
pages.text: Behind the dragon's bed lies a shed scale ten times the size of its own. Something far bigger once slept here. It may yet come home.
